test: does cross-line transfer improve with more cell lines?
log: LOOP 265 -- DOES CROSS-LINE TRANSFER IMPROVE WITH MORE CELL LINES?
Loop 264 ruled out the comfortable explanation: constraining the operator raised
its reliability 0.448 -> 0.611 and bought -0.0004 of transfer. A MORE reliable
operator transferring WORSE means the line-specificity is real, not noise.
One hypothesis is left and it is about DATA: nine lines may be too few to span
the space an unseen line lives in. 20 lines were extracted; 9 were ever used.
TRAP DECLARED FIRST: loop 262's span test fits coefficients on the held-out
line's OWN residual, so it is monotone in n BY CONSTRUCTION and a rising curve
would mean nothing. Coefficients here are fitted on HALF the held-out line's
genes and scored on the other half, which can and should turn over.

R7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
The new lines are thin. NPC and ASC carry about a quarter of the genes the
original nine do, so their operators are estimated from fewer rows and R3 is
the gate that says whether that mattered.
R4's slope is measured over n up to the lines available here. A curve that is
flat from 2 to 11 could still rise at 50; the honest claim is only that lines
OF THIS KIND, added at this rate, do not help.
NPC and ASC are not cancer lines, which is what makes them a real spanning test,
but it also means a failure could be distance rather than count -- they may be
too far from the nine to interpolate rather than too few.
